anthropic.notes: Cache-hit cost = base_input x cache_read_multiplier (0.1x standard, 0.025x on Fable 5.1/Mythos 5.1). A cache hit pays for itself after 1 read (5m TTL, 1.25x write) or 2 reads (1h TTL, 2x write). Multipliers stack: batch x cache x data-residency all compose multiplicatively. Only Claude Sonnet 4.5 among currently-billed models carries the >200K long-context premium; every model from the 4.6 generation onward (and Fable 5/5.1) gets the full 1M window at flat standard pricing per Anthropic's own pricing-page text. Opus 4.1 and earlier cap hard at 200K context (no >200K tier at any price).

openai.cached_input_note: Cached-input price varies per model, typically ~10x cheaper than base input (exact ratio varies: e.g. gpt-5.6-sol 10x, gpt-4o only 2x, gpt-3.5-turbo/gpt-4-turbo/gpt-4/legacy models show no cached-input discount at all on the current pricing page).
openai.notes: batch_discount and flex_discount (0.5x) and priority_multiplier (2.0x, now branded 'Fast mode' via service_tier:'fast' or the legacy 'priority') reflect OpenAI's long-standing, well-documented general policy and were NOT individually re-itemized per current model on the live pricing page this session (the page showed tab headers 'Standard | Batch | Flex | Fast mode' for the GPT-5.6 family but only the Standard tab's numbers were captured) -- treat batch/flex/priority columns in the models array as inferred from this general rule, not independently verified per model. Data-residency/regional-processing endpoints carry a 10% uplift for models released on/after 2026-03-05. GPT-5.6 Sol specifically carries promotional pricing confirmed through at least 2026-11-21.

google.context_cache_read_multiplier_note: Cache-read price is consistently exactly 10% of base input price across every Gemini model checked this session (e.g. Gemini 2.5 Pro $1.25 to $0.125; Gemini 3.8 Flash $0.75 to $0.075) -- NOT the 0.25x figure suggested in the task's schema skeleton. That 0.25x figure was not observed on any live page this session.
google.notes: Only the 'Pro'-tier reasoning models (3.1 Pro Preview, 2.5 Pro) carry a >200K long-context price premium (2x input, 1.5x output, 2x cache-read); every Flash-tier model checked has flat pricing regardless of context length. Non-global (regional) endpoints carry a 10% surcharge, taking effect for GA Gemini-3+-family non-global endpoints starting 2026-07-01 (global pricing applied to non-global before that date). Grounding queries: Gemini 3.x models use a cheaper $14/1000 rate with a shared 5,000/month free allowance; Gemini 2.0/2.5 models use the older $35/1000 (Search) / $45/1000 (Web Grounding Enterprise) structure with daily free allowances instead of monthly.

xai.notes: Every current xAI model checked shows exactly 2x input AND 2x output above 200K tokens (unlike Anthropic's differentiated 2x/1.5x split, or Google's Pro-only premium) -- a uniform doubling. xAI's entire model-naming generation has shifted since early 2026 (grok-4.6/4.5/4.3/4.20/4.1-fast/build-0.1 replacing grok-4/grok-3/grok-3-mini/grok-code-fast-1, none of which remain on the current docs.x.ai models page).

deepseek.notes: DeepSeek uniformly doubles ALL prices (cache-hit input, cache-miss input, output) during the peak UTC window above; off-peak (all other hours, i.e. most of the week) is the 'base' price used in the models array. deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner (the classic aliases many cost trackers still log) were retired 2026-07-24 in favor of deepseek-v4-flash/deepseek-v4-pro -- any pricing-catalog consumer matching on the old names needs a migration/fallback rule.
